events.title: Deadliest Earthquake in Recorded History Strikes Shaanxi
events.description: A catastrophic earthquake devastated the Wei River Valley in China's Shaanxi province. Many people lived in cave dwellings carved into loess cliffs, and these collapsed in huge numbers. Estimates of the dead run as high as about 830,000.
events.significance: It is generally regarded as the deadliest earthquake ever recorded. It later shaped understanding of seismic risk and building practices in vulnerable regions.

events.title: Elizabeth Blackwell Becomes America's First Woman Physician
events.description: Elizabeth Blackwell received her medical degree from the Medical Institution of Geneva in New York. She was the first woman in the United States to earn one.
events.significance: Her achievement opened the medical profession to women. She went on to found institutions that trained female doctors.

events.title: The Trieste Reaches the Bottom of the Ocean
events.description: Jacques Piccard and Lt. Don Walsh descended in the bathyscaphe Trieste to the floor of the Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench. They reached a record depth of about 10,911 metres (35,797 feet).
events.significance: It was the first crewed descent to the deepest known point on Earth. It showed that humans could reach the deepest parts of the ocean.

events.title: The 24th Amendment Is Ratified
events.description: South Dakota became the 38th state to ratify the 24th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution, completing the ratification process. The amendment banned poll taxes in federal elections.
events.significance: It removed a financial barrier that had been used to keep many Black and poor Americans from voting. It was an important step in the civil rights era.
